basis: The benchmark's output definitions hold (reference_audit/2026-09-28 rule 3), reading 'mandatory employee state payroll taxes' as the amount the law requires of the employee. An output-scope adapter applies that reading, in the form of latest_md_local_output_scope.py.

regenerated.basis: The output's definition counts mandatory employee state payroll taxes and excludes employer payroll taxes. Minnesota Paid Leave premiums "accrue and become payable by each employer" (Minn. Stat. 268B.14, subd. 1); the employer must pay at least 50 percent (small employers: at least a quarter of the full rate, subd. 5a), and employees pay through wage deductions only "the remaining portion, if any, of the premium not paid by the employer" (subd. 3), so the employee share runs from 0 to 0.44% of wages at the employer's choice. The frozen reference counts the largest share the employer may deduct (mn_employee_paid_leave_contribution $127.60); the regenerated value leaves it out and keeps employee Social Security and Medicare tax.

The output's definition counts mandatory employee state payroll taxes and excludes employer payroll taxes. Colorado FAMLI premiums are remitted by the employer (C.R.S. 8-13.3-507(2)), which "may deduct up to 50 percent of the premium" from wages (507(5)); an employer that deducts less is considered to have elected to pay the rest (7 CCR 1107-1 s. 1.4(6)(A)). The frozen reference counts the largest share the employer may deduct (co_employee_famli_contribution $17.99); the regenerated value leaves it out and keeps employee Social Security and Medicare tax.

The output's definition counts mandatory employee state payroll taxes and excludes employer payroll taxes. Massachusetts PFML contributions are remitted by the employer (M.G.L. c. 175M, s. 6(a)), which may deduct up to 100 percent of the family and 40 percent of the medical contribution from wages (s. 6(c)) and may choose to deduct less (458 CMR 2.05(5)(c)). The frozen reference counts the largest share the employer may deduct (ma_employee_paid_leave_contribution $805.01); the regenerated value leaves it out and keeps employee Social Security and Medicare tax.

The output's definition counts mandatory employee state payroll taxes and excludes employer payroll taxes. New York's covered employer must provide disability and Paid Family Leave coverage; it pays the disability cost beyond what it collects (N.Y. Workers' Compensation Law s. 210(1)), no employer is required to fund Paid Family Leave (s. 209(3)(b)), and the employer "is authorized to collect" employee contributions up to the statutory caps by payroll deduction (s. 209(4)). The Workers' Compensation Board says an employer "is allowed, but not required" to collect them. The frozen reference counts the largest share the employer may deduct (ny_employee_disability_benefits_contribution $31.20, ny_employee_paid_family_leave_contribution $411.91); the regenerated value leaves it out and keeps employee Social Security and Medicare tax.
